title: Carpentry, Kansas Vocational Institute and band teacher William L. Dawson
summary: Intending architecture, Thomas studies carpentry at the Tuskegee-style Kansas Vocational Institute, whose first band teacher, William L. Dawson, has a beautiful trombone tone.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Right. Now, guess who my first band teacher was! Man, how I got involved in music... My father wanted me to be an architect. So I went to school, and they had carpentry there, and I figured mechanical drawing, and carpentry was the nearest thing to me getting into architecture, because an architect needs know how to build, what to use as stones and all that. So I studied carpentry with Mr. Burke.
I'm trying to think now how I got involved... Oh. William L. Dawson was our first band teacher .
Yeah. He came there. He came right... I think he came right out of Tuskegee.
Now, what was the name of this school you went to?

Kansas Vocational Institute. That was the first name. Then they changed it later, when they added a couple of college studies... They changed it to Kansas Vocational College. Now, it was a state-supported school for Blacks only. The name of the college that was in Topeka was Washburn. And of course, you could go to any of the colleges. But this was a high school set up s a trade school, and it was set up on the way that Tuskegee was.

Because we had... I can't remember exactly, but we had four or five teachers from Tuskegee. And I guess that's how we got ahold of Dawson, because when they found out we needed a band teacher, they got him. He was a young teacher down there in Tuskegee...

And do you know, that man influenced me on tone? He had the most gorgeous tone on trombone I had ever heard... Well, I hadn't heard many trombone players anyway. And he kept his trombone shined; it looked like it was gold.
